themes.disagreements: While feature 126 is a very strong treatment predictor, its lack of outcome signal suggests it may be an instrument rather than a confounder.
themes.interpretation: Candidates exhibiting high support across univariable and forest models for both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis, suggesting potential confounding roles.
themes.name: Strong Treatment and Outcome Predictors

themes.disagreements: Feature 124 also shows moderate signals in main treatment and outcome models, which may overlap with its effect modification signal.
themes.interpretation: Candidates where the most credible signals appear in effect-estimation models (R-learners, Causal Forests) rather than main effect models.
themes.name: Treatment-Heterogeneity Signals

themes.disagreements: Feature 123 shows a penalized main treatment signal, but lacks the complementary outcome or effect signals required for a more active role.
themes.interpretation: Candidates with low overall support or signals primarily limited to outcome prognosis without strong treatment prediction or effect modification.
themes.name: Weak or Prognostic-Only Signals
